The test image shows a plant stem with:
- Whitish/bleached lesion on the stem
- Small black structures (likely sclerotia) scattered on the white tissue
- Stem girdling/canker
- Another segment on the right showing white-bleached stem tissue

Top candidates: **Southern_Blight** (white mycelium + sclerotia on stem), **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** (white mycelium + black sclerotia), **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**.

Now I'll view one reference from each of 8 different classes:

This reference (ID 1572826) is an excellent match to the test image (ID 1572832 - consecutive Bugwood numbers from the same series). Both show:
- Stem sections covered in white mycelial growth
- Small dark sclerotia forming on the white mycelium
- Green stem tissue still visible underneath the white growth

This is a strong visual match for **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**.

**Summary of evidence:**
- Test image: bleached white stem section with small black sclerotia, held against black background (Bugwood ID 1572832)
- `Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot/Bugwood_23.jpg` (ID 1572826): identical presentation — stems with white mycelium and developing black sclerotia, consecutive Bugwood numbers from same series
- Southern_Blight references showed more fluffy white mycelium at root zone, less matching
- Alternaria references showed darker blackened cankers, not white mycelium
- Gray_Mold showed fruit infection, not stem
- Sclerotinia sclerotia reference showed isolated large black structures
